title: How a 5-Step Checklist Cut Hospital ICU Infections by 66%
alt_title_1: Peter Pronovost's 2006 Study: Why Experts Still Need Checklists
alt_title_2: Stop Trusting Memory Under Stress: The Michigan ICU Rule
description_hook: In 2006, Johns Hopkins physician Peter Pronovost tested a five-step central-line hygiene checklist across 103 Michigan ICUs and empowered nurses to stop doctors who skipped a step, cutting bloodstream infections by up to 66%.

scenes.headline: Five Plain Checkboxes Beat Expensive Medical Tech
scenes.stat_label: MICHIGAN ICU INFECTION DROP OVER 18 MONTHS (2006)
bullets: Tested by Johns Hopkins physician Peter Pronovost
Zero new drugs or hardware: just a 5-step sterile checklist
scenes.narration: In 2006, Johns Hopkins physician Peter Pronovost cut deadly intensive-care bloodstream infections by up to sixty-six percent across Michigan without inventing a single new drug or surgical device.
scenes.source: Peter Pronovost et al., New England Journal of Medicine 355:2725 (2006)

scenes.headline: 103 ICUs Hit a Median Infection Rate of Zero
bullets: 5 basic steps: handwash, drapes, skin prep, vein site, removal
Nurses got explicit authority to stop doctors who skipped one
scenes.narration: Tracking 103 Michigan ICUs across 1,981 ICU-months, Pronovost introduced five basic central-line steps and gave nurses full authority to stop any doctor who skipped one. Within three months, the median infection rate dropped to zero.
scenes.source: Peter Pronovost et al., New England Journal of Medicine 355:2725 (2006)

scenes.headline: Urgency Makes Even Elite Experts Skip Steps
scenes.left_body: High IQ + time pressure -> silent skipped steps & costly bugs
scenes.right_body: Written pre-flight check -> catches dumb mistakes in 30 seconds
scenes.narration: Experienced physicians already knew all five sterile rules by heart, yet urgency and fatigue caused silent skips. Solo operators fail the exact same way when rushing code deployments, tax filings, or portfolio trades from memory.
scenes.source: Peter Pronovost et al., New England Journal of Medicine 355:2725 (2006)

scenes.headline: Gate Every Irreversible Action With 5 Written Lines
scenes.narration: Write a mandatory five-line pre-flight checklist for every irreversible workflow in your calendar, and refuse to wire funds, ship code, or place orders until all five boxes pass.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Peter Pronovost et al., NEJM (2006)

scenes.headline: Checkboxes Beat Raw Willpower Under Pressure
scenes.stat_label: EXTERNALIZE CRITICAL STEPS OUT OF WORKING MEMORY
bullets: Keep checklists short: 5 killer items on a single index card
Give your checklist hard authority to halt any rushed launch
scenes.narration: Stop trusting raw memory under stress, because five boring checkboxes outperform hurried brilliance every single week.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Peter Pronovost et al., NEJM (2006)
